reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is to transform a stochastic, high-dimensional deployment process into a controlled, verifiable sequence of binary decisions. Feature flags act as a coarse-grained proxy for the continuous state of the system, reducing the complexity of rollback to a simple flip operation. However, this reduction introduces a new class of failure: flag misfires. To mitigate this, we introduce a gate function that enforces consistency constraints, effectively pruning the state space to a safe subset. The rollback kernel then serves as a corrective mechanism that pushes the system back toward this safe region when deviations occur. Together, these operators form a closed-loop control system that trades off exploration (innovation) against exploitation (stability). The risk reduction iso-surface provides a quantitative metric for tuning the aggressiveness of the control, balancing the probability of catastrophic failure against the utility of new features.
